title: kube-provisioning-playground-commands-log
content:
Personal scratchpad for the provisioning flake seen on playground clusters (mostly ephemeral test nodes). Not a final runbook — breadcrumbs + commands I ran and quick hypotheses.

Summary of symptom:
- Fresh nodes join cluster but quickly go NotReady or show kubelet CrashLoopBackOff.
- On some machines kubelet starts and then OOMs when containerd pulls large images.
- Others show long delays in kubeadm join due to timeouts contacting control-plane.
- Repro intermittent; seems correlated with concurrent node boots (burst provisioning) and NVMe provisioning on certain instance types.

Environment notes:
- cluster: playground-dev (k8s 1.27.3), control-plane on t3a.xlarge equivalent in test cloud region-us-west2; nodes are ephemeral spot-like instances.
- provisioning: cloud-init -> kubeadm join (kubeadm v1.27) -> install calico via helm (local chart) -> kube-proxy
- image cache warm/unwarm varies; some nodes fall back to pulling many images at once.

Commands tried (copied shell transcript style):

# Check node and events
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide
NAME                           STATUS   ROLES    AGE    VERSION
ip-10-0-1-12.ec2.internal      NotReady  <none>  6m     v1.27.3

$ kubectl describe node ip-10-0-1-12.ec2.internal
...
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----    ------     ---   ----               -------
  Warning NetworkUnavailable 4m kubelet            route not ready: 192.168.0.0/16
  Warning NodeNotReady 2m kubelet           Kubelet stopped posting node status.

# kubelet logs on the node (journalctl)
$ ssh ubuntu@10.0.1.12 'sudo journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager -n 200'
Feb 14 09:42:11 ip-10-0-1-12 kubelet[2540]: E0214 09:42:11.123456   2540 eviction_manager.go:755] eviction manager: failed to get pod stats: *stats.Error{Err:"failed to get rootfs info: failed to stat /var/lib/kubelet/pods: no such file or directory"}
Feb 14 09:42:11 ip-10: kubelet[2540]: Fatal error: failed to start container runtime: timed out waiting for the condition

# containerd status
$ ssh ubuntu@10.0.1.12 'sudo ctr -n k8s.io containers ls'
ctr: failed to connect: failed to dial "/run/containerd/containerd.sock": context deadline exceeded

# cloud-init output (first-boot errors)
$ ssh ubuntu@10.0.1.12 'sudo cat /var/log/cloud-init-output.log | tail -n 80'
...
WARNING: cloud-init[2279]: Unhandled error: apt-cache failed updating package lists (temporary network DNS glitch?)
ERROR: cloud-init[2279]: kubeadm join --token REDACTED --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:... failed: timed out after 120s contacting control-plane

# kubeadm join retry trace
$ sudo kubeadm join 10.0.0.11:6443 --token REDACTED --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:... --v=5 2>&1 | tee /tmp/kubeadm-join.log
I0214 10:01:02.123456  1234 util.go:75] [bootstrap] created cluster-info configmap
I0214 10:01:45.654321  1234 join.go:235] discovery failed: failed to discover master: Get "https://10.0.0.11:6443/version": dial tcp 10.0.0.11:6443: i/o timeout

Error snippets I copied:
- "failed to get rootfs info: failed to stat /var/lib/kubelet/pods: no such file or directory"
- "failed to dial \"/run/containerd/containerd.sock\"": context deadline exceeded
- "kubeadm join ... failed: timed out after 120s contacting control-plane"
- "eviction manager: failed to get pod stats"
- cloud-init apt-cache update warnings leading to delayed package installs

Hypotheses so far:
1) Networking during initial boot (DHCP/DNS) is flaky when many instances spin up; cloud-init apt/ssh and kubeadm attempts happen before network stable.
2) containerd not ready because overlayfs/aufs mount failed due to missing kernel module which wasn't installed yet (apt delayed).
3) NVMe init/race: ephemeral NVMe devices not fully initialized leading to /var/lib/kubelet mountpoint missing at time kubelet starts.
4) Token discovery timeouts caused by network egress or control-plane briefly saturated during burst provisioning.
5) Some images are very large and concurrent pulls OOM the node — kubelet evicts critical components.

Quick checks to collect when repro-ing:
- systemd unit statuses: sudo systemctl status kubelet containerd cloud-init --no-pager
- journal for last 200 lines: sudo journalctl -u kubelet -u containerd -u cloud-init -n 200 --no-pager
- mount and disk: lsblk; sudo mount | grep kubelet; sudo stat -c '%U %G %a' /var/lib/kubelet || true
- fd usage: sudo lsof /run/containerd/containerd.sock || true
- active apt operations: ps aux | grep -E 'apt|dpkg' && sudo tail -n 80 /var/log/apt/term.log

Mini script I ran to atomically gather diagnostics (useful to run from bootstrap script after failure):

COLLECT=/tmp/node-provision-diagnostics-$(date +%s).tgz
mkdir -p /tmp/diag && \ 
  sudo journalctl -u kubelet -u containerd -u cloud-init -n 500 --no-pager > /tmp/diag/journals.txt 2>&1 || true && \ 
  sudo lsblk > /tmp/diag/lsblk.txt 2>&1 || true && \ 
  sudo mount > /tmp/diag/mounts.txt 2>&1 || true && \ 
  sudo stat -c '%U %G %a %n' /var/lib/kubelet 2>/tmp/diag/kubelet.stat || true && \ 
  sudo ctr -n k8s.io containers ls > /tmp/diag/ctr-containers.txt 2>&1 || true && \ 
  tar czf $COLLECT -C /tmp diag || true && echo "diag:$COLLECT"

Notable one-off experiments I tried (and results):
- Delay kubelet start: systemctl disable kubelet; add sleep 60 in cloud-init before enabling kubelet -> lower failure rate in bursts. Suggests timing/race.
- Precreate /var/lib/kubelet and chown root:kubelet 0755 in cloud-init early -> removed rootfs stat errors on subsequent boots.
- Increased kubeadm discovery timeout to 10m for join -> made some joins eventually succeed but hides root cause.
- Force containerd restart on boot if socket missing (systemd oneshot) -> helped for some nodes where containerd started too slowly.

Helm install related note (observed after node joined):
- helm upgrade --install calico ./charts/calico -n kube-system --values my-values.yaml
Observed helm hook timeouts when nodes under memory pressure; logs: "Error: rendered manifests contain a resource that already exists" (race: chart hooks running during partial cluster state).

Immediate mitigations to try next:
- In cloud-init: ensure apt updates + required kernel modules installed before enabling kubelet/containerd; add retries/timeouts around apt-get update.
- Add small jitter to node bootstrap start (random sleep 30-120s) to avoid thundering herd.
- Precreate kubelet directories and ensure proper SELinux/context if enabled.
- Use a small init-container image pull pre-warm step before kubelet enabling (pull smaller images first).
- Telemetry: add metric on time from instance ready -> kubeadm joined and kubelet Ready to catch distribution.

Longer-term ideas:
- Move kubeadm join off cloud-init and into a rate-limited controller that sequentially enrolls new nodes (plays nicer with control-plane).
- Investigate switching container runtime to a less heavy default for ephemeral spot nodes where disk/ram are tight.
- Add preboot health check for NVMe devices and ensure mounts are ready before kubelet starts.

Things to avoid in a quick patch: increasing discovery timeout is bandaid. We want to address race order and thundering herd.

Notes / TODO (short):
- Add a cloud-init patch that creates /var/lib/kubelet, sets ownership, and retries apt-get 5x with backoff.
- Run a small experiment: provision 30 nodes w/ jittered start vs simultaneous to measure failure rate.
- Collect 10 tarballs from failed nodes and upload into INFRA-842 ticket.
- Try using systemd 'Requires=containerd.service' for kubelet unit override to enforce ordering.

References/quick links I kept in Slack during triage:
- slack thread: #infra-node-burn 2026-02-15 (search for 'provision burst')
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/k8s-provisioning/pull/118 (early retry logic)

End of scratchpad. Will refine into a formal runbook if mitigation experiments show a single dominant cause.
